h1: Practice management software for dental clinics
coreKeyword: practice management software for dental clinics
secondaryKeywords: dental practice management system, dental clinic scheduling software, patient billing software for dentists
contentIdea: Show that Chairside is built around how a dental clinic actually runs a day, rather than being generic scheduling software with a dental label on it. The argument is that scheduling, recall and insurance eligibility belong on one patient record, and that everything the front desk loses time on comes from those three living apart.
productDescription: Chairside is practice management software for independent and small-group dental clinics. Scheduling, patient recall, real-time insurance eligibility checks and patient billing all run off one patient record. It is used mainly by practices running 2 to 12 operatories, including multi-location groups that share a hygiene schedule across sites. Migration comes from Dentrix and Open Dental backups and takes about 14 days from contract to the first live appointment. Pricing is per operatory from $149 per operatory per month with unlimited user seats.
clientProof: Northgate Dental cut its no-show rate from 14% to 6% in the first quarter after switching on waitlist auto-fill (2025, https://chairside.example.com/customers/northgate-dental). Ridgeway Family Dentistry recovered $47,000 in unscheduled hygiene recare across three locations in six months (2025, https://chairside.example.com/customers/ridgeway). Platform-wide first-pass claim rejection rate is 2.1% for the 12 months to March 2026. Customers include Northgate Dental, Ridgeway Family Dentistry, Coastline Dental Group and Fairmount Pediatric Dental. Priya Raman, Practice Manager at Northgate Dental: "We stopped calling the insurer to check benefits. The check is already on the appointment when the patient walks in."
certifications: HIPAA compliant (third-party audited), SOC 2 Type II, PCI DSS Level 1
ctaRules: Name Chairside explicitly in the closing CTA and tie it to the clinic's own schedule. Offer the no-show recovery checklist as the lower-commitment option. Never promise a specific no-show reduction to a prospect, only report what named customers measured.
writingPreferences: Address the reader as "you" and assume they run or manage the practice. Say "clinic" rather than "office". Never use the word "solution" as a noun. Do not use the phrase "dental professionals".
